headline: Discovery reveals what exists but was unknown—pulling back the curtain on reality's hidden features
universal_truth: Truth exists before we find it; our job is to look carefully enough to see
fun_facts: Gravity existed for billions of years before Newton 'discovered' it—the apple fell long before anyone understood why
Many scientific discoveries were made by accident while looking for something else
Some discoveries require new technology to even be possible—microscopes revealed microbes that were always there
discussion_questions: What's the difference between discovery and invention?
What might exist right now that nobody has discovered yet?
What have you 'discovered' about yourself that was always there?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Gravity didn't start working when Newton described it. Germs caused disease before anyone knew they existed. Discovery is different from invention—you're not creating something new, you're finding what was already there, hidden in plain sight.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Discovery reveals existing reality, while invention creates new reality. But discovery isn't passive—it requires active searching and often new ways of looking. What does discovery actually involve?

options.text: Discovery requires attention, curiosity, and often new tools or perspectives that let us see what was previously invisible
options.response: Yes. Discoveries aren't lying on the surface—they require penetrating vision, persistent investigation, and sometimes new instruments. The reality was there; the seeing had to be developed.

options.text: Discovery happens when we stumble upon new things
options.response: Serendipity plays a role, but discovery usually requires systematic investigation...

q1.title: Tools Reveal Truths
q1.script: The telescope revealed distant planets that were always there. The microscope revealed microbes. X-rays revealed bones inside bodies. Many discoveries required new tools—not to create reality but to finally perceive it.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Tools Reveal Truths"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Prepared Minds
q2.script: Louis Pasteur said 'chance favors the prepared mind.' Accidental discoveries often happen to people who recognize their significance. Fleming noticed mold killing bacteria; others had seen it before but didn't understand what they were seeing.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Undiscovered Country
q3.script: Much remains undiscovered. We've mapped more of the moon than the ocean floor. Most species haven't been catalogued. Dark matter and dark energy are names for things we know exist but don't understand. Reality exceeds our knowledge.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Truth exists before we find it. Discovery teaches that our job is to look carefully enough to see what's already there—in science, in others, in ourselves.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 170—170 days of learning! Tomorrow, we'll explore going where no one has been—exploration. Until then, look carefully at something familiar; what might be hiding there?
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Attention Practice - See What's Hidden
growTrack.activity: Look at something familiar—a room, a person, a routine—with fresh eyes. What have you never noticed? What patterns exist that you've overlooked? Discovery happens when we attend carefully to what's already there but unseen.
